title: Jump first (Sotah 37a)
hookLine: the tribes hesitate at the sea; Nachshon jumps in first
tomorrow: Joseph's coffin is lost somewhere in Egypt. who still knows where?

cards: A wedding, the music's on, and the dance floor is empty. Everyone is at the edges, holding a drink, waiting. Nobody wants to be first.
Then one person walks out alone, a little awkward, and within a song the floor is full. The Talmud tells that moment at the edge of the Red Sea, with a lot more water.

teach.b: Egypt's army behind them, water in front. Rabbi Yehuda says each tribe stood at the edge saying: not me first.
Then Nachshon, son of Amminadab, of the tribe of Judah, jumped in, and the water rose to his neck.
Meanwhile Moses was praying at length, and God answered him with Exodus: "Wherefore criest thou unto Me? speak unto the children of Israel, that they go forward."
Right beside that, Rabbi Meir tells it the other way: the tribes raced to be first, and Benjamin got there. The Talmud keeps both. Nachshon's is the version people repeat.
Here's one to tell a friend tonight: in this telling, the sea doesn't split so people can step in. Someone steps in, and then it splits. Now this week's neighbor.
Christians tell a story with the same wet feet. In Matthew's Gospel, Jesus comes walking on the water toward his disciples' boat and says, Come.

teach.h: PETER: COME DOWN OUT OF THE SHIP.
teach.b: "And when Peter was come down out of the ship, he walked on the water, to go to Jesus."
What's shared is the step itself: leaving the safe place before the water makes sense. And an honest difference.
Peter steps out because Jesus calls him, and when he begins to sink, Jesus catches him; Christians read it as a story of trusting Jesus.
Nachshon goes uncalled, while Moses is still praying, and the Talmud reads his jump as the moment a whole people starts to move. Two stories, one shared courage: going first.

how: In Jewish speech a 'Nachshon' is someone who goes first, and the crossing of the sea is read aloud in synagogue during Passover and in the weekly Torah cycle. Christians read Peter's walk on the water in Matthew 14.

o: leap to conclusions before you hear both sides
go in first, before the way is clear
cross over the sea on dry ground, as Moses did

games.q: at the edge of the water — tap the pairs.
p: jumps in before the sea splits
told: speak, that they go forward
steps out of the boat when Jesus says come

s: in this telling, the sea split first and then the people walked in
Nachshon steps in first, the water up to his neck, and then it splits.
the Talmud gives only one answer to who went first
Rabbi Yehuda says Nachshon of Judah; Rabbi Meir says Benjamin. it keeps both.
in Matthew, Peter steps onto the water because Jesus says come
Peter is called; Nachshon goes uncalled. both leave the safe place first.

games.q: your group project is stuck: everyone agrees the topic is wrong, but nobody wants to tell the teacher. by Nachshon's story, what gets things moving?
o: you email the teacher first, and invite the others to add their names.
you wait for the group leader, since going first is a leader's job.
you keep talking it over until everyone is ready to go together.
games.why: the tribes waited at the edge, each saying not me. Nachshon jumped, and God told Moses: speak, that they go forward. once someone steps in, the rest can follow.

practice: Stand up, if you can, feet together, as if at the edge of the water. Name one thing you've been waiting for someone else to start: an apology, a plan, a hard conversation.
Take one step forward, and with it decide the first small move you'll make. Stay standing there, on the far side of the step, while the sit runs.

wordCard.voice: Jump first: Nachshon at the sea, in the water to his neck before it split, so the others could follow.

orig.note: Hebrew name: Nachshon son of Amminadab, of Judah, who in the Talmud jumps in first.

carryVoice: Your line: jump first. Others start moving once someone does. Thirty-five down, five to go.

sources.ref: Babylonian Talmud, Sotah 37a (Rabbi Meir: Benjamin went down first; Rabbi Yehuda: each tribe refused until Nachshon son of Amminadab jumped in; Moses praying at length)
